title: Shanghai AI Lab Open-Sources Intern-Decision, Small Models That Output Decisions, Not Text
key_facts: Shanghai AI Lab open-sourced Intern-Decision, small models of 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters, released on 28 Sep per Pandaily.
They return a structured answer with probabilities (choice, score or yes/no) instead of long text, in one forward pass.
They fine-tune the language part of Qwen3.5 and can take images as input, shown on game and browser tasks.
The lab says the 4B model averages 90.02% accuracy over seven test suites, 1.28 points above Jev (88.74%), a commercial reference model.
Latency is about 44 milliseconds on a single RTX 4090; the figures are self-reported.
Training data is not included; weights are on Hugging Face; chipmaker MetaX announced Day-0 support.
quote_evidence: Instead of producing long passages of text, the models are built to return a structured judgment directly, together with probabilities for each possible answer.
These figures are self-reported by the developers, and the repository notes that evaluation protocols and scope differ between models.
why_it_matters_hint: Small decision models could make automated choices cheaper and easier to audit.
notes: Page text read from the article data embedded in the Pandaily page. Release dated 28 Sep, so stale; score lowered 5 to 4.
